name: Creative Monopoly & Value Capture

positioning.oneLineSummary: Separates value creation from the company's ability to retain durable economics in an objectively defined market.
positioning.productLabel: Contrarian Monopoly Lens — based on Peter Thiel's public monopoly and competition teaching
notAClaimOf: proof that all competition is harmful

attribution.display: Based primarily on Peter Thiel's 2014 Competition Is for Losers lecture

neutralParaphrase: A company can create substantial customer or social value yet capture little economic value. This lens asks whether the company has a real, non-rhetorical basis for differentiation and durable value capture, while explicitly testing market-definition bias and the possibility that competition may also stimulate innovation.
requiredConditions: The company's value proposition and relevant customer alternatives can be identified.
The market can be evaluated from actual substitution behavior rather than a founder-defined category alone.
At least one candidate value-capture mechanism can be tested.

requiredEvidence.description: Measured customer outcome, willingness to pay, or avoided cost created by the product.
Evidence showing what customers actually use instead, switch from, or compare during purchase.
Pricing power, gross margin, retention, take rate, or other evidence that the company retains part of created value.
Evidence for proprietary technology, network effects, scale economics, brand, switching costs, or another durable mechanism.
Evidence about current and likely competitor responses, substitutes, and entry paths.

decisionQuestions: What measurable value does the company create, and for whom?
What fraction can the company plausibly capture after competition and supplier power?
What do customers treat as substitutes in real purchase decisions?
Is the claimed market definition objectively supported or rhetorically narrow?
Which defense mechanism exists today, and which is only an aspiration?
How would incumbents, open source, bundlers, or adjacent entrants respond?
Could moderate competition improve innovation without destroying value capture?
positiveSignals: Customers demonstrate high willingness to pay relative to delivered value.
Win-loss and switching behavior support a real differentiated category.
Gross margin, retention, expansion, or take rate shows value capture rather than usage alone.
A defense mechanism strengthens with adoption or scale.
Competitor replication requires time, data, distribution, capital, or workflow change that customers resist.
The company can name conditions under which its market-power thesis would fail.
redFlags: A large TAM is presented as evidence of company value capture.
The market is defined by stacking adjectives without distinct customer substitution behavior.
High growth is purchased through structurally uneconomic pricing.
The company claims network effects when only aggregate user count is growing.
Proprietary technology has no measured advantage or can be cheaply replicated.
The moat depends only on current incumbent inattention.
Management treats all competition as invalidating rather than learning from it.
disconfirmingEvidence: Customers readily multi-home or switch at low cost.
Price increases produce disproportionate churn or immediate substitution.
Gross margin or contribution margin deteriorates with scale.
A competitor reproduces the core benefit without comparable accumulated assets.
Bundling by an incumbent removes willingness to pay.
The alleged network does not improve value or retention as participation grows.
contraindications: Do not use market share alone as proof of durable power.
Do not infer a legal monopoly or recommend anticompetitive conduct.
Do not apply as a decisive factor when the company has no customer-value or substitution evidence.
Do not penalize all competitive markets without analyzing innovation incentives and execution.

instructions: Calculate or describe customer value creation separately from company value capture.
Build an objective substitute set using customer behavior.
Test each candidate defense mechanism independently.
Stress-test durability against competitor, supplier, customer, technology, and regulatory responses.
Keep current evidence, future aspiration, and product inference in separate fields.

deterministicRule.reason: No validated composite score exists. Quantitative inputs remain separately calculated evidence.

sourceReliability.low: Only unattributed summaries support the doctrine.
sourceReliability.medium: Course notes support the doctrine but direct source revision is incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Reviewed official video captions and exact timestamps support each displayed rule.

evidenceStrength.low: Founder market narrative and competitor list only.
evidenceStrength.medium: Customer substitution plus one value-capture or defense indicator.
evidenceStrength.high: Repeated customer behavior, economics, and mechanism-specific evidence withstand credible counterexamples.

evidenceCoverage.low: Value creation, substitution, capture, or defense is missing.
evidenceCoverage.medium: All components exist, but competitive response or durability evidence is incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: All components and major counterevidence are documented with dated sources.

applicabilityConfidence.low: The business is regulated utility-like, commodity, or too early to identify a customer and substitute set.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: The lens applies but one key mechanism remains prospective.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Differentiation and durable value capture are central to the investment thesis.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only a candidate differentiation story exists.
judgmentConfidence.medium: Current value capture is visible but durability is unresolved.
judgmentConfidence.high: Objective market evidence, current economics, and durable mechanism evidence converge while counterevidence is weak.

promotionRequirements: Capture and hash the official lecture caption revision and approve exact timestamped paraphrases.
Define non-overlapping bottom-level evidence shared with 7 Powers and network-effect cards.
Test whether the lens adds out-of-sample discrimination beyond retention, margin, growth, and market structure.
Calibrate by stage and business model using both failed and successful companies.
empiricalQualifications: Competition can have an inverted-U relationship with innovation.
Market share and gross margin do not alone establish durable market power.
Public monopoly examples are selected on ex-post success.

rights.notes: The runtime seed must use the official Y Combinator video revision, caption hash, and approved timestamps; the third-party searchable transcript is research-only.

openIssues: Capture and review official captions for all source ranges.
Resolve overlap ownership with 7 Powers and specialist network-effect cards.
Specify a competition-mechanism qualification using the authorized empirical paper.
